title: Introduce heatmap-based warmth curves and quantization fallback orchestrator
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Cold-prefill behavior and tenant burst characteristics vary widely across tenants. We introduce a compact heatmap-based "warmth curve" representation to capture tenant prefill affinity over time and request shape, plus a quantization fallback orchestrator that uses those warmth curves plus runtime latency signals to pick a safe quantization profile at inference time. Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost by applying aggressive quantization where safe, while avoiding user-visible latency or quality regressions during bursty or previously unseen traffic patterns. This PR implements the runtime orchestrator, a lightweight heatmap generator, Console + CLI knobs for rollout, and an e2e simulation harness for policy validation.

merge_commit_message:
Introduce heatmap warmth curves and quant-fallback orchestrator

- heatmap generator and exporter
- runtime orchestrator + policy graph
- console + CLI knobs
- telemetry and e2e simulator

Rollout: gradual, feature-flagged; default off for short-lived tenants.
release_notes: Adds tenant warmth heatmaps and a quantization fallback orchestrator that selects quant profiles based on prefill affinity and runtime latency signals. New Console controls for rollout and per-tenant opt-out. Telemetry: new prefills/heatmap histograms and quant-fallback events. Default rollout: feature-flagged and disabled for tenants with <30 days of traffic.
testing_notes: - Unit tests covering decision graph edge cases; - e2e simulation with three adversarial burst profiles; - perf bench compares PQ8 / FP16 paths under mixed workloads; - CI gate requires perf-bench and e2e-sim to pass; flaky e2e-sim rerun included.
backport_plan: Not backported. This feature is behind a feature flag and will be enabled via a staged rollout. If necessary, a cherry-pick to release branches can be prepared after additional validation.
how_to_rollout: 1) Enable feature-flag in Console for a small tenant cohort; 2) Monitor prefills_heatmap and quant_fallback_event metrics for quality regressions; 3) Expand to 25% then 100% over weeks; 4) If perf or quality issues observed, toggle fallback to conservative quant profiles or disable per-tenant via opt-out
notes_on_risk: Medium: changes decision-making for quant profiles at runtime. Mitigations: default conservative profiles, per-tenant opt-out, telemetry alerting on latency/quality drift, automatic fallback to FP16 on sustained tail latency degradation.
examples_of_runtime_behavior: - Tenant A: heatmap shows strong prefill affinity during business hours; orchestrator applies PQ8 for cost savings while keeping KV-prefill enabled. - Tenant B: sparse, bursty traffic with short history: orchestrator opts for conservative FP16 and keeps warmup prefills on to avoid regressions.
notes: This PR focuses on safe automation for cost-optimization; follow-ups planned: (1) auto-tuning of heatmap bucket widths, (2) integrating model-eval quality signals into the decision graph, (3) a lightweight simulation CLI for customers to preview settings.
